title: Accountability
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Accountability is the loving practice of helping one another walk in the light through confession, correction, encouragement, and prayer. Biblical accountability is not control, but faithful care under God’s Word.
summary: Accountability is the loving practice of helping one another walk in the light through confession, correction, encouragement, and prayer. Biblical accountability is not control, but faithful care under God’s Word.
christFocus: Jesus Christ brings His people out of darkness into light and shepherds them through truth and grace. Accountability serves His restoring work by helping believers resist sin and follow Him faithfully.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers are not called to fight sin alone. Scripture commands God’s people to restore the fallen gently, confess sins, pray for one another, exhort one another, and bear burdens.

Accountability requires humility. A person must be willing to be known, corrected, encouraged, and helped. Pride hides sin, but grace brings it into the light.

Accountability also requires love and wisdom from those who give it. Correction should not be harsh, controlling, or self-righteous. It should aim at restoration and faithfulness.

Healthy accountability helps prevent hardening. Daily encouragement and honest correction can protect believers from deceitful sin and spiritual drift.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people remain trapped because secrecy protects sin. Others fear accountability because they have experienced control or shame. Scripture gives a better way: truth in love for restoration.

This doctrine helps recovery, discipleship, and church life become more faithful. God often uses other believers as instruments of grace to help His people endure.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Invite faithful believers into your life who will tell you the truth and pray with you. Confess sin honestly, receive correction humbly, and offer help gently. Do not use accountability to control others; use it to help one another follow Christ.
